Car Rental Insurance in Albania Explained: CDW vs Super CDW in Plain Language

20 November 2026 6 min read

When you rent a car in Albania, basic insurance called CDW usually limits what you pay for damage to a fixed amount, the excess. Super CDW reduces that excess, often to zero, so a scratch or dent does not turn into a large bill. Below we explain the terms in plain language, what is usually excluded and how to protect yourself at pickup and return.

The three insurance terms you need to know

Third-party liability

Every car registered in Albania must have compulsory third-party liability insurance. It covers damage or injury you cause to other people and their property. It does not cover damage to the rental car itself, which is where CDW comes in.

CDW (Collision Damage Waiver)

CDW is not insurance in the strict sense. It is an agreement in which the rental company waives most of the cost of damage to the car, as long as you follow the rental terms. You remain responsible for a fixed amount called the excess (also known as the deductible). If damage costs less than the excess, you pay the repair cost. If it costs more, you pay only up to the excess.

At Rent Ride, basic CDW is included in the price of every car at no extra cost.

Super CDW (zero excess)

Super CDW is an optional upgrade that reduces your excess. With Rent Ride, Super CDW means no excess at all on covered damage. You pay a little more per day and, in return, you do not have to worry about the cost of a covered dent or scrape. We especially recommend it for Albania's narrow coastal roads, mountain passes and busy city parking.

What is usually not covered

Every rental company defines its own exclusions, so always read your rental terms before signing. Across the industry, the following are commonly excluded or covered only under specific conditions:

  • Tyres and wheels, including punctures and damaged rims
  • Glass, such as the windscreen, windows and mirrors
  • Undercarriage damage, for example from driving on rough tracks or hitting rocks
  • Lost or damaged keys
  • Interior damage, such as stains, burns or torn seats
  • Wrong fuel put in the tank
  • Damage caused by driving under the influence, by an unauthorised driver, or by breaking the rental agreement, for example crossing a border without permission

These exclusions matter most if you plan to drive unpaved roads. Before heading somewhere remote, ask whether the road is suitable for your car. Our guide to driving in Albania covers road conditions in more detail.

Can I rely on my credit card's rental insurance?

Some credit cards include rental car cover, and it can be useful. However, there are important caveats:

  • It is often reimbursement-based. You may have to pay the rental company first and then claim the money back from the card issuer, with paperwork.
  • Country exclusions. Some card policies exclude certain countries, including countries outside the EU. Check whether Albania and any country you plan to visit are covered.
  • Vehicle exclusions. Luxury cars, large SUVs or vans are sometimes excluded.
  • Conditions apply. Many policies require you to pay for the whole rental with that card.

Read your card's policy document, not just the marketing summary, and contact your card issuer if anything is unclear. Many travellers simply choose a zero-excess option from the rental company because claims are handled locally and quickly.

How to avoid damage disputes

Most disagreements about damage come down to one question: was that scratch there before? A few simple habits protect you completely.

At pickup

  1. Walk around the car with the staff member and point out every mark, however small.
  2. Record a video on your phone, slowly circling the car. Include the wheels, bumpers, windscreen and roof if you can see it.
  3. Take close-up photos of existing scratches and dents, with the date visible on your phone.
  4. Photograph the dashboard to record the fuel level and mileage.
  5. Check that existing damage is noted on the rental agreement before you sign.

During the rental

  • If anything happens, however minor, call the rental company straight away and follow their instructions.
  • In an accident involving another vehicle, call the police and get a written report. Insurance claims usually require it.
  • Park in well-lit or guarded areas when possible, and never leave valuables visible.

At return

  • Return the car in daylight if you can, and inspect it together with the staff member.
  • Take another quick video and a photo of the fuel gauge.
  • Keep your photos and videos until any final invoice is settled.
  • If the staff member notes any new damage, ask for it to be written down and photographed together, so both sides agree on exactly what was found.

Insurance and deposits

With many rental companies, a high excess comes with a large security deposit blocked on your credit card. That can tie up a significant part of your holiday budget. Rent Ride requires no security deposit, which makes budgeting simpler. You can pay by cash or card. If you want the same peace of mind for damage, simply add Super CDW when you book.

Driving abroad? Check your cover

If you plan to visit Kosovo, North Macedonia, Greece or another neighbouring country, the car needs cross-border permission and valid insurance documents for each country. Read our guide to crossing borders with a rental car from Albania before you go.

Frequently asked questions

Is CDW mandatory when renting a car in Albania?+

Third-party liability insurance is compulsory for every car, and rental companies normally include it. CDW, which limits your liability for damage to the rental car, is usually offered as standard or as an option depending on the company. At Rent Ride basic CDW is already included in every rental price, so you are not asked to pay extra for it.

What is the difference between CDW and Super CDW?+

With basic CDW you still pay up to a fixed excess if the car is damaged. Super CDW is an optional upgrade that lowers that excess; with Rent Ride it removes the excess completely on covered damage. Both are subject to the exclusions in the rental terms, so always read what is and is not covered before you sign.

Does Super CDW cover tyres and windscreens?+

It depends on the company. In the rental industry, tyres, glass, undercarriage and keys are frequently excluded or covered only under certain conditions, even with a zero-excess option. Check the rental terms for your specific booking, or ask the company directly before pickup so there are no surprises if something happens.

Should I buy Super CDW for a road trip in Albania?+

For most road trips it is worth considering. Coastal roads, mountain passes and tight parking in towns increase the chance of small scrapes, and a zero-excess option means a minor incident does not become a large bill. If your trip is short and mostly on motorways, basic CDW may be enough for some drivers.
